jurisdiction.name: Bulgaria
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Bulgaria's AI policy rests on the 2020 Concept for the Development of AI in Bulgaria until 2030. EU AI Act implementation is led by the Ministry of e-Government: a June 2025 Council of Ministers decision designates the authorities protecting fundamental rights under the Act, and a national bill on the use and development of AI was introduced in parliament in September 2026. The Institute of Public Administration published a voluntary ethics code for AI in the state administration and an AI readiness index, and the Financial Supervision Commission has a paper on AI in the non-bank financial sector.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The 2025 designation decision and the education ministry's AI guidelines are marked as located but not fully checked, and the pending AI bill is listed as a lead to check later.

instruments.official_title: Доброволен кодекс за етично използване на изкуствен интелект в държавната администрация
instruments.english_title: Voluntary Code for the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in the State Administration
instruments.summary: Voluntary code drafted by the Institute of Public Administration that state institutions can sign to commit to responsible, transparent and lawful use of AI. It applies to AI systems an institution uses or commissions, including systems supporting administrative decisions, data analysis, generative models and citizen-facing tools, and sets principles such as public interest and fundamental rights, legality and proportionality, transparency and labelling of AI use, and human oversight and accountability. IPA publishes the code it signed, a template for other institutions and a list of adopting bodies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main public-sector AI ethics instrument for the Bulgarian state administration.
instruments.current_status: Published on the IPA site on 30 June 2026 (signed IPA code and adoption template). Voluntary; the IPA list of adopters names IPA and the municipalities of Burgas and Bansko. IPA states the document is open to future changes.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): IPA page (dated 30 June 2026) and 8-page code PDF read (pdftotext); adopter list read on IPA network page

instruments.official_title: Public Administration AI Readiness Index, Bulgaria 2025
instruments.english_title: Public Administration AI Readiness Index, Bulgaria 2025
instruments.summary: First AI readiness index for Bulgarian public administration, published by the Institute of Public Administration, built from an online survey of 6,254 civil servants (22 April - 9 May 2025) combining organisational and individual readiness on a 0-100 scale. It puts overall readiness at 45/100 ('building capacity'), notes that institutions have not yet taken concrete steps to prepare for the EU AI Act and that only 18% of respondents report an institutional AI policy or guidance, and recommends management commitment, training and open-data measures.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Government-published AI readiness assessment of the state administration.
instruments.current_status: English edition (machine-translated and expert-reviewed) of the IPA 2025 index; revised version August 2026 with recalculated indicator coding. The Bulgarian original is published by IPA.

instruments.official_title: Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Bulgaria until 2030
instruments.english_title: Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Bulgaria until 2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Transport, Information Technology and Communications
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Transport, Information Technology and Communications
instruments.summary: Bulgaria's national AI strategic document ('Artificial intelligence for smart growth and a prosperous democratic society'), prepared by MTITC from Bulgarian Academy of Sciences drafts of 2019-2020. It sets measures in areas such as reliable AI and data infrastructure, research capacity, skills, support for innovation, awareness and trust, and a regulatory framework for trustworthy AI in line with international regulatory and ethical standards, and lists possible priority sectors. Implementation is to be coordinated by MTITC through an Interdepartmental Working Group that prepares an operational National Plan/Roadmap with measures, deadlines and indicators.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Bulgaria's only national AI strategy document; no successor strategy has been published.
instruments.current_status: Official English version (cover dated October 2020) published by MTITC. The Bulgarian draft 'Проект на Концепция за развитието на изкуствения интелект в България до 2030 г.' was in public consultation on strategy.bg (No. 5337-K) from 19 August to 18 September 2020. Not yet verified from the official text: adoption by the Council of Ministers on 16 December 2020. No successor strategy found; the AI bill submitted to the National Assembly on 24 September 2026 (see leads) would provide for a national AI strategy.

instruments.english_title: Council of Ministers Decision No. 398 of 18 June 2025 designating the public authorities under Article 77(2) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act)
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers decision implementing Article 77 of the EU AI Act by designating the national public authorities that supervise or enforce EU fundamental-rights obligations (including non-discrimination) for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III. It instructs the Minister of e-Government to notify the European Commission and the other Member States of the list and to publish it on the Ministry of e-Government website.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only located national act implementing the EU AI Act's governance provisions in Bulgaria.
instruments.current_status: Council of Ministers decision located on the government's legal information portal (pris.government.bg); its title wording, number, date and list of designated bodies still need checking against the official text. Not yet verified from the official text: designation of market surveillance authorities under the AI Act. The September 2026 AI bill addresses them.

instruments.official_title: Изкуствен интелект в небанковия финансов сектор /проучвания, анализ, насоки/
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence in the Non-Bank Financial Sector (studies, analysis, guidance)
instruments.summary: Discussion paper by the Financial Supervision Commission on AI in the insurance, investment and pension-insurance sectors. It outlines the European Commission's April 2021 AI Act proposal (prohibited practices, high-risk classification, provider obligations), sets out four risk tasks for firms deploying AI (risk identification, assessment, prevention and control), and reports the results of an FSC survey of supervised entities on their use of AI, including their call for practical AI guidance and communication with the supervisor.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only AI-specific document found from a Bulgarian financial supervisor.
instruments.current_status: PDF published on fsc.bg, dated 2021 on the cover. Non-binding; no later FSC AI guidance found.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National law, the government, ministries and regulators were searched. No qualifying documents were found for procurement, cybersecurity, data and privacy, standards, regulatory sandboxes, drafts, international instruments or historical publications. Several official sites, including those of the data protection commission and the e-government ministry, were unavailable, so their AI material and the Convention 108 ratification law remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The 2025 designation decision and the education ministry's AI guidelines could only be located because their websites timed out or blocked access, and the pending AI bill is listed as a lead.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. cpdp.bg TLS chain/503, egov.government.bg and mee.government.bg 502/reset/503, mon.bg 403, pris.government.bg document pages timed out (Decision 398/2025 and MON guidelines located only from the search index). Convention 108 ratification act (2002) not found on an official site. Units covered: Law: parliament.bg bills API (52nd National Assembly, all bills filtered for AI): one pending AI bill (lead). strategy.bg consultations searched: 2020 draft AI Concept consultation (event on the Concept record); no AI law or AI-specific provisions in adopted laws found. Council of Ministers Decision No. 398/2025 under AI Act Art. 77 located on pris.government.bg (located only). State Gazette not searched issue by issue; no AI Act market-surveillance designation act found.; Government: MTITC/MTC (Concept until 2030, reviewed), Institute of Public Administration (voluntary ethics code, readiness index, reviewed), Council of Ministers portal pris.government.bg (decision pages time out). Ministry of e-Government site unreachable (502/503). No successor AI strategy and no central public-sector GenAI guideline found.; Ministries: Education (MON 2024 school AI guidelines, located only: mon.bg 403). Health, justice, defence, finance/tax, labour, interior: searched via web search, nothing AI-specific found.; Regulators: FSC (2021 AI discussion paper, reviewed). CPDP: cpdp.bg failed (TLS chain error on curl, 503 on WebFetch), no CPDP AI guidance found via search. BNB, CRC, CPC, cyber authority: searched, nothing AI-specific found.. Not reached: CPDP website (cpdp.bg: TLS certificate chain error on curl, HTTP 503 on WebFetch); Ministry of e-Government website (egov.government.bg / mee.government.bg: proxy 502/connection reset, WebFetch 503); mon.bg (HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch); pris.government.bg document pages (timeouts); State Gazette (dv.parliament.bg) search for the 2002 Convention 108 ratification law.
